note_sections.t: Re-evaluation for treatment decision following diagnosis of high-grade prostate cancer.

Long-standing referral for prostate cancer management. The patient is a 60-year-old retired civil servant, married, and resides independently in a retirement community. He reports moderate lower urinary tract symptoms with an IPSS of 10. He is alcohol-free and maintains a regular exercise routine, running 5 km three times weekly. Medical history includes hypercholesterolaemia managed with statin therapy. He is an ex-smoker with a 20 pack-year history, having quit in 2014. Recent PSA trend shows a rapid rise from 4.2 ng/mL in June 2023 to 19.0 ng/mL in January 2025. He has no significant occupational hazards or recent travel history.

On DRE, the prostate is symmetrically enlarged without palpable nodules, consistent with clinical stage cT1c. General examination reveals a well-nourished man with stable vital signs, BP 139/70 mmHg, HR 71 bpm. No lymphadenopathy or abdominal masses are detected.
